newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end narrowly mixed in late downturn.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end narrowly mixed in late downturn.

text.p: A late bout of profit-taking in Kuala Lumpur shares brought blue chips off their best levels and tipped secondary shares into the minus column at the close. Volume was robust.
"We're not seeing any particular strong seller," said Ralph Dixon, of TA Securities' international division. "I think it's fairly mixed in terms of profit-taking across the board."
The Composite Index of large-capitalised stocks ended up 2.04 points to 1,264.90, after hitting a new intraday 1,272.30 session high. The Second Board fell 3.61 points to 647.08.
Volume was the heaviest so far this year, at over 927 million shares. Interest stayed on lower-valued stocks. Property and timber shares were among the more popular buys.
"It's probably a lot of syndicates starting things up," said an institutional dealer, referring to the speculative pools of money that ramp up stock prices.
"Timber has been a laggard sector," he said.
Talk of takeovers and asset injections stirred up the group, dealers said. Within the industry, Sinora Industries jumped 1.00 to 13.80 ringgit and Aokam Perdana gained 44 cents to 4.92.
